turns.content: A rational number is called short when its decimal expansion terminates. Characterize short rational numbers in terms of the prime factors that may remain in a reduced denominator.
Apply that criterion to (10^t-1)/(cm) and express the first qualifying exponent using an additive order rather than a multiplicative order.
Count the integers c in {1,...,2017} that are coprime to 10, and use this to prove an upper bound for |S(m)|.
Let P be the primes p<=2017 other than 2 and 5. Choose alpha so that every p in P divides 10^alpha-1, and set m=10^alpha-1. Explain why this construction is suitable for attaining the upper bound.
Using the lifting-the-exponent valuation identity, prove that ord_{cm}(10)=c alpha for every admissible c, so these orders are all distinct.
Combine the upper bound and the attaining construction to report the maximum possible value of |S(m)|.
